text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- The Warsaw-based Bank Handlowy's (BH) net profit was 556 million zlotys in 1996 and its return on capital reached 33 percent. The bank has been earmarked for privatisation this year and the results should spur investors to buy its shares, BH said.
- The cabinet will soon discuss a modified project for the KRP Poludnie petrochemical complex development in southern Poland, which will cost $3 bilion.
- Poland's food prices increased 2.5 percent in December, the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said.
- Germany's Eurowings airlines launches daily flights between Dusseldorf and Wroclaw today, Eurowings said.
- The Gdynia-based Polish Navy shipyard has launched its first 1900 deadweight tonnage (DWT) tanker vessel contracted by a Norwegian shipowner.
- The Lodz-based food caterers and restaurant-owners have formed an association to promote improved service standards and conduct professional trainings for the catering service sector.
NOWA EUROPA

- Politicians from Poland's Conservative Party (PK), Christian-Peasant Party (SLCH) and the right-wing deputies who left the centrist Union for Freedom (UW) have formed a new centre-right party, called Conservative-Christian Alliance (SKL). The new party will join the AWS Solidarity right-wing bloc to challenge the ruling ex-communists in this year's parliamentary elections.
- Poland's consumer credits grew by 104.4 percent in 1996. the National Bank of Poland (NBP), the central bank said.
- Interest on 12-month deposits will decrease from 19.76 percent to 18.78 percent in mid-year, according to a banking survey.
- Poland's cement production will grow this year by 1.4 percent and by 2.8 percent in 1998, the Central Statistical Office (GUS) and the Bank Handlowy Capital Operations Centre (BH COK) said.
- The construction of a new oil reloading facility in the Gdansk Port Polnocny port will start in spring this year. The facility's annual reloading capacity will be 12 million tonnes, the port said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- Poland's annual juice consumption was 11 litres per capita in 1996. Since 1993 the consumption has grown by 400 percent, the Instytut Ekonomiki Rolnictwa, an agricultural economy institute, said.

- Telekomunikacja Polska (TPSA), the state-owned telecom monopolist will soon invite bidders interested in the telephone chipcard production. The contract will be worth about $150 million, Gazeta Wyborcza learnt unofficailly.

- Romania owes Poland $7.3 million and the debt's return is a condition for Poland's support of Romania's access to the Central European Free Trade Association (CEFTA), the Bucharest-based Polish commercial counsellor Grzegorz Matusiewicz said.
ZYCIE

- The Magna Polonia National Investment Fund (NFI) will not list any of its member companies on the Warsaw bourse and will concentrate on their restructuring this year. It may introduce some of the firms on the over-the-counter (OTC) market, the fund's management consortium president Witold Radwanski said.
